title: How many presses of plus one thousand make one lakh?
description: A calculator in the Land of Tens has only a plus one thousand button. The video finds the presses for several numbers by dividing by one thousand, and shows what one hundred fifty three presses make. Keeko raises a hand, thinking that ten presses make a lakh.
teaching_notes: One idea: with a button that adds one thousand, the number of presses is the number divided by one thousand. Ask the class how many thousands one lakh holds before anyone divides. Watch for students who copy the presses for ten thousand and use them for one lakh.

source: Thoughtful Thousands has only a +1000 button. How many times should it be pressed to show: (a) 3000, (b) 10,000, (c) 53,000, (d) 90,000, (e) one lakh, (f) the number shown by 153 presses, (g) the thousands needed to make one lakh
video_script.why: The child knows that a lakh is ten ten thousands and can divide a multiple of one thousand by one thousand.
video_script.substitution: A button that adds one thousand is pressed as many times as there are thousands in the number, so the presses are the number divided by one thousand.
video_script.anchor: A calculator has only a plus one thousand button: how many presses show one lakh?
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko copies the ten presses that show ten thousand and uses them for one lakh. A lakh is ten times ten thousand, so it needs ten times the presses, which is one hundred.
video_script.payoff_line: One lakh needs one hundred presses
never_show: the +1 or +10 buttons of the other calculators
maths_rules: the slip: ten presses show ten thousand, not one lakh
video_script.design: One idea: presses of a plus one thousand button are the number divided by one thousand. Wrong idea: Keeko reuses the ten presses of ten thousand for a lakh. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the presses for each number. We also find the number shown after one hundred fifty three presses.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, divide each number by one thousand. Three thousand needs three presses, and ten thousand needs ten presses.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Fifty three thousand needs fifty three presses, and ninety thousand needs ninety.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, go the other way. Each of one hundred fifty three presses adds one thousand, so multiply by one thousand.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The screen shows one lakh fifty three thousand.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 1,00,000 ÷ 1000 = 100 presses; one lakh holds 100 thousands
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>For one lakh, divide by one thousand. One lakh holds a hundred thousands.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One lakh needs one hundred presses.
